question: Let $f$ be a real-valued differentiable function defined on the real line $\mathbb R$ such that its derivative $f\prime$ is zero at exactly two distinct real numbers $\alpha$ and $\beta$. Then,

options.A: $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are points of local maxima of the function $f$.
options.B: $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are points of local minima of the function $f$.
options.C: one must be a point of local maximum and the other must be a point of local minimum of $f$.
options.D: given data is insufficient to conclude about either of them being local extrema points.
